chapter.name: Central Council of Ministers
chapter.blurb: The Union Council of Ministers under Articles 74, 75, 77, 78 and 88: ministerial advice, appointment and oath, collective and individual responsibility, composition, council versus cabinet and the kitchen cabinet.

source.title: Indian Polity (question set written from its topics)

concepts.name: Constitutional provisions: Articles 74, 77, 78, 88 and the nature of ministerial advice

questions.q: Under Article 78 of the Constitution, it is the duty of the Prime Minister to
questions.a: communicate to the President all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to administration and proposals for legislation
o: communicate to the President all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to administration and proposals for legislation
countersign every order issued by the President in the exercise of a public act and answer for it in the courts
administer the oaths of office and secrecy to the other ministers on behalf of the President before they take charge
frame the rules for the allocation of business among the ministers on his own authority without reference to the President
questions.e: p.316: Article 78 makes it the Prime Minister's duty to communicate to the President all Council decisions on administration and legislative proposals, to furnish information the President calls for, and to submit a matter on the President's requirement.
w: Countersignature of the President's orders is not required in India (p.318).
The oaths are administered by the President (p.315, p.317), not by the Prime Minister.
The rules for allocation of business are made by the President under Article 77(3) (p.316).

questions.q: According to Laxmikanth, the provision that the nature of advice tendered by ministers to the President cannot be enquired into by any court emphasises
questions.a: the intimate and confidential relationship between the President and the ministers
o: the intimate and confidential relationship between the President and the ministers
the personal discretion of the President to disregard ministerial advice
the immunity of the Council of Ministers from the control of the Lok Sabha
the final authority of the Prime Minister over the decisions of the cabinet
questions.e: p.316: Article 74(2) bars courts from enquiring into the advice, which emphasises the intimate and confidential relationship between the President and the ministers.
w: Advice is binding on the President (p.316); the bar protects confidentiality, not discretion.
Collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha continues (p.318); the bar is only about courts.
The bar concerns the President-minister relationship, not the Prime Minister over the cabinet (p.316).

questions.q: In U.N.R. Rao case (1971), the Supreme Court held that after the dissolution of the Lok Sabha the Council of Ministers
questions.a: does not cease to hold office
o: does not cease to hold office
ceases to hold office on the date of dissolution
continues to hold office only in a caretaker capacity of one month
holds office only if the President personally so directs
questions.e: p.316: the Court held that even after dissolution of the Lok Sabha the Council of Ministers does not cease to hold office, and that Article 74 is mandatory.
w: The Court held the opposite: the council does not cease to hold office (p.316).
The chapter gives no one-month limit; the council simply does not cease to hold office (p.316).
Article 74 is mandatory; the President's personal direction is not the test (p.316).

questions.q: In Shamsher Singh case (1974), the Supreme Court held that wherever the Constitution requires the satisfaction of the President, that satisfaction is
questions.a: the satisfaction of the Council of Ministers, with whose aid and advice the President acts
o: the satisfaction of the Council of Ministers, with whose aid and advice the President acts
the personal satisfaction of the President, formed after consulting the Chief Justice of India
the satisfaction of the Lok Sabha, expressed through a resolution passed by a majority of its members
the satisfaction of the Prime Minister alone, apart from the rest of the Council of Ministers
questions.e: p.316: in Shamsher Singh the Court held the satisfaction is not personal to the President but that of the Council of Ministers.
w: The Court expressly said it is not the personal satisfaction of the President (p.316).
No resolution of the Lok Sabha is involved (p.316).
The Court spoke of the Council of Ministers as a body, not of the Prime Minister alone (p.316).

questions.q: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 amended Article 74 to provide that the President shall, in the exercise of his functions,
questions.a: act in accordance with the advice rendered by the Council of Ministers
o: act in accordance with the advice rendered by the Council of Ministers
act in accordance with the advice only after the Lok Sabha has approved it
require the Council of Ministers to reconsider its advice once before acting
consult the Chief Justice of India before acting on the advice
questions.e: p.323 (footnote 1): the 42nd Act made the President act in accordance with the advice; the reconsideration proviso came only with the 44th Act of 1978.
w: No approval by the Lok Sabha is mentioned (p.323).
The reconsideration proviso was added later, by the 44th Act (p.323).
No consultation with the Chief Justice is mentioned (p.323).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 77 (Conduct of Business of the Government of India):

1. The validity of an order authenticated in the specified manner shall not be called in question on the ground that it was not made or executed by the President.
2. The rules for the allocation of Government business among Ministers are made by the Prime Minister.
3. All executive action of the Government of India is expressed to be taken in the name of the President.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 77(2) (p.316). Statement 2 is incorrect: the President makes the rules (p.316). Statement 3 is correct: Article 77(1) (p.316).
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.316
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.316
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.316

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 78 (Duties of Prime Minister):

1. It is the duty of the President to communicate to the Prime Minister all decisions of the Council of Ministers.
2. The Prime Minister must furnish such information about Union administration and legislative proposals as the President may call for.
3. If the President so requires, the Prime Minister must submit for the Council's consideration a matter on which a minister has decided but the Council has not deliberated.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the duty to communicate is the Prime Ministers, towards the President (p.316). Statement 2 is correct: Article 78(2) (p.316). Statement 3 is correct: Article 78(3) (p.316).
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.316
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.316
'3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.316

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the amendments to Article 74 (Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President):

1. The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 amended Article 74 so that the President shall act in accordance with the advice of the Council of Ministers.
2. The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 added a proviso allowing the President to require reconsideration of the advice.
3. After such reconsideration the President shall act in accordance with the advice tendered.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.323 footnote 1. Statement 2 is correct: p.323 footnote 1. Statement 3 is correct: p.316 and footnote 1.
w: '1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.323
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.323
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.323

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court cases mentioned in the chapter:

1. In U.N.R. Rao case (1971) the Court held that the Council of Ministers does not cease to hold office even after dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
2. In Shamsher Singh case (1974) the Court held that the satisfaction of the President means the satisfaction of the Council of Ministers.
3. In U.N.R. Rao case the Court held that, once the Lok Sabha is dissolved, the President may exercise executive power without the aid and advice of the council.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.316. Statement 2 is correct: p.316. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Court held Article 74 mandatory and such exercise unconstitutional (p.316).
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.316
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.316
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.316

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the rights of ministers as respects the Houses of Parliament:

1. A minister who is a member of the Lok Sabha has no right to speak in the Rajya Sabha.
2. A minister who is a member of the Rajya Sabha may vote in the Lok Sabha on a no-confidence motion.
3. Under Article 88 every minister may speak in a joint sitting of the Houses.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: he has the right to speak and take part in the other House too (p.317). Statement 2 is incorrect: a minister can vote only in the House of which he is a member (p.317). Statement 3 is correct: Article 88 covers either House, a joint sitting and committees (p.316).
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.317
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.317
'1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.317

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Constitution requires an order of the President for a public act to be countersigned by a minister.
2. Courts are barred from enquiring into the nature of advice rendered by ministers to the President.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: there is no such requirement in India (p.318). Statement 2 is correct: Article 74(2) (p.316, p.318).
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and omits statement 2, which is correct: there is no such requirement in India (p.318).
'Both 1 and 2' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: there is no such requirement in India (p.318).
'Neither 1 nor 2' omits statement 2, which is correct: Article 74(2) (p.316, p.318).

questions.q:
The chapter has a table of Articles related to the Central Council of Ministers. Consider the following:

1. Article 74 - Council of Ministers to aid and advise President.
2. Article 75 - Other provisions as to Ministers.
3. Article 77 - Duties of Prime Minister as respects the furnishing of information to the President.
4. Article 88 - Rights of Ministers as respects the Houses.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Table 21.2 (p.322). Statement 2 is correct: Table 21.2 (p.322). Statement 3 is incorrect: that is Article 78; Article 77 is conduct of business (p.322). Statement 4 is correct: Table 21.2 (p.322, 323).
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.322
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.322
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.322

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Constitutional scheme of the parliamentary system:

1. The principles of the parliamentary system are not detailed in the Constitution, but Articles 74 and 75 deal with them in a broad and general manner.
2. Article 74 deals with the appointment, tenure and oath of ministers, while Article 75 deals with the status of the Council of Ministers.
3. The Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister is the real executive authority in the politico-administrative system.
4. The parliamentary system of the Constitution is modelled on the American pattern.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.315. Statement 2 is incorrect: the two are swapped (p.315). Statement 3 is correct: p.315. Statement 4 is incorrect: it is modelled on the British pattern (p.315).
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.315
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.315
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.315

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 75 (Other Provisions as to Ministers):

1. The salaries and allowances of ministers shall be determined by Parliament.
2. The President shall administer the oaths of office and secrecy to a minister.
3. The Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to both Houses of Parliament.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 75(8) (p.315). Statement 2 is correct: Article 75(6) (p.315). Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 75 makes it collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (p.315).
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.315
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.315
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.315

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 88:

1. Every minister has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of either House.
2. The right extends to any committee of Parliament of which the minister is named a member.
3. The right under Article 88 includes voting at a joint sitting of the Houses.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.316. Statement 2 is correct: p.316. Statement 3 is incorrect: he is not entitled to vote under Article 88 (p.316). So exactly 2 correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct.
'All three' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 77:

1. Orders authenticated under rules made by the President cannot be questioned on the ground that the President did not make them.
2. The validity of such an authenticated order may be questioned on the ground that it was not executed by the President.
3. The rules for the transaction of Government business are made by Parliament.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.316. Statement 2 is incorrect: the validity shall not be called in question (p.316). Statement 3 is incorrect: the President makes them (p.316). So exactly 1 correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct.
'All three' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 75:

1. The total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.
2. A minister who is not a member of Parliament for any period of six consecutive months shall cease to be a minister.
3. The ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the Prime Minister.
4. A member disqualified on the ground of defection is also disqualified from being appointed a minister.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.315. Statement 2 is correct: p.315. Statement 3 is incorrect: they hold office during the pleasure of the President (p.315). Statement 4 is correct: p.315. So exactly 3 correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The council of ministers headed by the Prime Minister is the real executive authority in the politico-administrative system.
Statement-II: Articles 74 and 75 deal with the principles of the parliamentary system in a broad, sketchy and general manner.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct (p.315). Statement-II is correct (p.315). The brevity of the two Articles is a separate remark and does not account for the council's role as real executive.
w: Rejected: The sketchy treatment of the principles in two Articles does not explain why the council is the real executive.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct (p.315).
Rejected: Statement-I is correct (p.315).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Council of Ministers does not cease to hold office on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
Statement-II: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Rajya Sabha.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: U.N.R. Rao (1971), p.316. Statement-II is incorrect: Article 75 makes the council collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (p.315).
w: Rejected: Statement-II is incorrect, so it cannot explain anything.
Rejected: Statement-II is incorrect.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct (p.316).

questions.q:
Match the Article in List-I with its subject in List-II.

List-I (Article)
A. Article 74
B. Article 75
C. Article 77
D. Article 78

List-II (Subject)
1. Duties of Prime Minister as respects furnishing information to the President
2. Council of Ministers to aid and advise President
3. Conduct of business of the Government of India
4. Other provisions as to Ministers
questions.e: Table 21.2 (p.322): 74 aid and advise; 75 other provisions as to ministers; 77 conduct of business; 78 duties of Prime Minister.
w: A and B are interchanged: 74 is aid and advise, 75 is other provisions.
C and D are interchanged: 77 is conduct of business, 78 is duties of the Prime Minister.
A and C are interchanged: 74 is aid and advise, 77 is conduct of business.

concepts.description: Articles 74, 77, 78, 88 and the binding nature of ministerial advice.
concepts.idea: Council of Ministers aids and advises the President, whose action on its advice cannot be examined by courts.
concepts.rule: Article 74 provides a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President, who shall act in accordance with such advice (p.315). The President may require reconsideration but must act on the advice tendered after it; the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 made the advice binding and the 44th Act of 1978 added the proviso (p.316, p.323). The advice tendered by ministers cannot be inquired into in any court (p.315, p.316). Article 77: executive action is expressed in the name of the President, authenticated orders cannot be questioned on that ground, and the President makes the rules for business and its allocation (p.316). Article 78 makes it the Prime Minister's duty to communicate Council decisions, furnish information and submit matters on the President's requirement (p.316). Article 88 lets a minister speak and take part in either House, a joint sitting and committees but not vote (p.316). In U.N.R. Rao (1971) the council did not cease on dissolution of the Lok Sabha and Article 74 was mandatory; in Shamsher Singh (1974) the President's satisfaction was held to be the council's (p.316).
concepts.example: A President who doubts advice may send it back once; after reconsideration he must act on it.

concepts.name: Appointment, oath, salary and size of the Council of Ministers (Article 75)

questions.q: The ceiling of 15 per cent on the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, is calculated on the total strength of the
o: two Houses of Parliament taken together
House of which the Prime Minister is a member
questions.e: p.315: the total number of ministers shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha (91st Amendment Act, 2003).
w: The base is the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya Sabha (p.315).
The base is the Lok Sabha alone, not both Houses (p.315).
The base is fixed as the Lok Sabha whichever House the Prime Minister belongs to (p.315).

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a part of the oath of office taken by a Union minister?
questions.a: to defend the Fundamental Rights against encroachment by the legislature
o: to defend the Fundamental Rights against encroachment by the legislature
to bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India
to uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India
to do right to all manner of people without fear or favour, affection or ill will
questions.e: p.317: the oath of office has four limbs (faith and allegiance, sovereignty and integrity, faithful discharge of duties, doing right to all without fear or favour). Defending Fundamental Rights against the legislature is not among them.
w: This is the first limb of the oath (p.317).
This is the second limb of the oath (p.317).
This is the fourth limb of the oath (p.317).

questions.q: According to Laxmikanth, the persons who are usually appointed as Union ministers are
questions.a: members of Parliament, belonging to either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha
o: members of Parliament, belonging to either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha
members of the Lok Sabha alone, since the council is responsible only to that House
members of the Rajya Sabha alone, since that House is never dissolved
persons recommended by the Speaker and approved by the Chief Justice of India
questions.e: p.317: usually members of Parliament, of either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha, are appointed ministers; a non-member can also be appointed for up to six months.
w: Rajya Sabha members are also appointed (p.317).
Lok Sabha members are also appointed; the usual pool is both Houses (p.317).
Ministers other than the Prime Minister are appointed on the Prime Minister's advice (p.317).

questions.q: According to Article 75, the salaries and allowances of ministers are determined by
o: the President on the advice of the Prime Minister
the Council of Ministers itself, by a resolution of the cabinet
the Finance Commission, through its periodic report
questions.e: p.315, p.317: Parliament determines the salaries and allowances of ministers from time to time, by the Salaries and Allowances of Ministers Act, 1952.
w: Parliament, not the President, determines them (p.315).
The council does not fix its own pay (p.315, p.317).
The chapter assigns the task to Parliament, not the Finance Commission (p.317).

questions.q: In 2001, the monthly sumptuary allowance of the Prime Minister was raised from Rs 1,500 to
questions.e: p.317: in 2001 the Prime Minister's sumptuary allowance rose from Rs 1,500 to Rs 3,000 per month.
w: Rs 2,000 is the new figure for a cabinet minister (p.317).
Rs 1,000 is the new figure for a minister of state (p.317).
Rs 6,000 is not a figure in the chapter; the Prime Minister's new figure is Rs 3,000 (p.317).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the appointment of ministers:

1. The Prime Minister is appointed by the President.
2. Other ministers are appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
3. The President may appoint as a minister a person not recommended by the Prime Minister if he thinks fit.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 75(1) (p.315). Statement 2 is correct: Article 75(1) (p.315). Statement 3 is incorrect: the President can appoint only those recommended by the Prime Minister (p.317).
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.315
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.315
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.315

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about a minister who is a member of the Rajya Sabha:

1. He has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of the Lok Sabha.
2. He can vote in the Lok Sabha.
3. He can vote in the Rajya Sabha.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.317. Statement 2 is incorrect: he can vote only in the House of which he is a member (p.317). Statement 3 is correct: p.317.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.317
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.317
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.317

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the oaths of a Union minister:

1. The President administers both the oath of office and the oath of secrecy.
2. In the oath of secrecy the minister swears not to reveal any matter brought under his consideration, except as required for the due discharge of his duties.
3. In the oath of office the minister swears to faithfully and conscientiously discharge the duties of his office.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.317. Statement 2 is correct: p.317. Statement 3 is correct: p.317.
w: '1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.317
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.317
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.317

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the salaries and allowances of ministers:

1. The salaries and allowances of ministers are fixed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
2. The Salaries and Allowances of Ministers Act of 1952 has been passed for this purpose.
3. A minister gets the salary and allowances payable to a member of Parliament.
4. Over and above these, a minister gets a sumptuary allowance according to rank.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: they are determined by Parliament (p.315, p.317). Statement 2 is correct: p.317, p.323. Statement 3 is correct: p.317. Statement 4 is correct: p.317.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.315
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.315
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.315

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 91st Amendment Act of 2003:

1. It added to Article 75 a ceiling of 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha on the Council of Ministers.
2. The ceiling excludes the Prime Minister from the count of ministers.
3. It also disqualified a member disqualified on the ground of defection from being appointed a minister.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.315. Statement 2 is incorrect: the total includes the Prime Minister (p.315). Statement 3 is correct: p.315.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.315
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.315
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.315

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 75:

1. The ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President.
2. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
3. A minister who is not a member of Parliament for any period of three consecutive months ceases to be a minister.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 75(4) (p.315). Statement 2 is correct: Article 75(5) (p.315). Statement 3 is incorrect: the period is six consecutive months (p.315).
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.315
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.315
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.315

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Deputy Prime Minister, in the context of Devi Lal's oath in 1990:

1. The Supreme Court upheld the oath as valid.
2. The oath was challenged because the Constitution provides only for the Prime Minister and ministers.
3. Describing a person as Deputy Prime Minister confers on him the powers of the Prime Minister.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.317. Statement 2 is correct: p.317. Statement 3 is incorrect: the description is descriptive only (p.317).
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.317
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.317
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.317

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about ministers who are not members of Parliament:

1. A person who is not a member of either House can be appointed a minister.
2. Such a minister must become a member of either House by election only, and nomination is not permitted.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.317. Statement 2 is incorrect: membership may come by election or nomination (p.317).
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and omits statement 1, which is correct: membership may come by election or nomination (p.317).
'Both 1 and 2' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: membership may come by election or nomination (p.317).
'Neither 1 nor 2' omits statement 1, which is correct: p.317.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Prime Minister.
2. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to Parliament as a whole.
3. The salaries and allowances of ministers are determined by Parliament.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: they hold office during the pleasure of the President (p.315). Statement 2 is incorrect: it is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (p.315). Statement 3 is correct: p.315.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.315
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.315
'1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.315

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about a minister who is not a member of Parliament:

1. He may be appointed a minister.
2. He must become a member of either House within six months.
3. He may become a member by election or by nomination.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.317. Statement 2 is correct: p.317, Art 75(7). Statement 3 is correct: p.317. So exactly 3 correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct.

concepts.description: Collective, individual and legal responsibility of ministers.
concepts.idea: The council swims or sinks together before the Lok Sabha while each minister serves at the President's pleasure.
concepts.rule: Article 75 makes the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha; all ministers, including those from the Rajya Sabha, resign when a no-confidence motion is passed, and the Prime Minister's resignation is the council's (p.318, p.323). The council may advise dissolution of the Lok Sabha, but the President may not oblige a council that has lost confidence (p.318). Cabinet decisions bind all ministers, and a dissenting minister who will not defend them must resign, as Ambedkar, Deshmukh and Arif Mohammed did (p.318). Ministers hold office during the President's pleasure, and the President removes a minister only on the Prime Minister's advice, even if the council enjoys confidence (p.318). India has no legal responsibility of ministers, no countersignature is needed, and courts cannot inquire into the advice, unlike Britain (p.318).
concepts.example: A minister who cannot defend a Cabinet decision resigns, as Arif Mohammed did over the 1986 Act.

concepts.description: Role of the Cabinet, writers' descriptions and the Kitchen Cabinet.
concepts.idea: The cabinet is the highest decision-making body, informally shadowed by the Prime Minister's inner circle.
concepts.rule: The cabinet is the highest decision-making authority, chief policy body, supreme executive authority, chief coordinator and crisis manager, controls higher appointments and deals with foreign affairs; its advice binds the President (p.321). Writers describe it as the steering wheel (Muir), keystone (Lowell), pivot (Marriott), solar orb (Gladstone), magnet of policy (Barker) and hyphen and buckle (Bagehot); Muir called its position a dictatorship only qualified by publicity (p.321). The Kitchen Cabinet is an informal, extra-constitutional inner circle of the Prime Minister that may include outsiders and was powerful under Indira Gandhi (p.322). Its merits are efficiency, speed and secrecy; its demerits lowered cabinet authority and bypassing the legal process; it also exists in the USA and Britain (p.322).
concepts.example: The Prime Minister takes a problem to a few trusted friends before the full cabinet meets.
